answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making every identity serve unpredictable jury duty on disputes drawn from an atlas of past cases. Each juror must attend unannounced sessions and defend a verdict, so one operator cannot staff many seats at once. Verdicts are scored against the basalt-hard evidence record, and a poor or missed verdict burns that identity's bond. Every extra identity on the same funding trail must post a bond larger by a fixed delta than the last, so each fake costs more outside money, more live hours, and another human who cannot attend two sessions at once.
